set.body:
Phase D (architecture). Two related boundary violations.

1. Client/server inversion. build.sbt:128-130 makes the CLIENT module depend on the SERVER module:
       lazy val ssh = project.dependsOn(core, protocol, agent, worker, testkit % "test->compile")
   and agent itself pulls in cli and local (build.sbt:116). ssh/Slurm.scala:8 imports agent.AgentApi, :13-14 imports worker.SlurmTaskCall and worker.SlurmBatch, and :36-38 declares RemoteSlurm extends AgentApi[F] — a client inheriting a server-side trait declared at agent/AgentService.scala:67-93. AgentCall/AgentFailure already live in protocol, which is where the transport-neutral contract belongs.

   Target: protocol (wire DTOs, limits, codecs, protocol client contract) / ssh client (core + protocol + CE/FS2) / agent (server assembly and target-side implementations) / task remote support (extensions over the protocol client, OUTSIDE the scheduler client) / worker (registered-task execution and result publication).

2. Kernel purity. ADR 0001 states "Cats Effect and FS2 are confined to interpreter/application modules". kernel/AtomicFiles.scala:30 exposes Sync operations and build.sbt:48 gives remote-exec-kernel a catsEffect dependency. ADR 0010 assigns atomic filesystem mechanics to the kernel, so the two ADRs are in tension and the code follows 0010. Split: a pure contract artifact and an effectful filesystem artifact. The artifact NAME matters less than moving filesystem mechanics and effect wrappers out of the neutral contract.

3. Remove the SharedKernel compatibility aliases (documented as removable in ADR 0010) before a first supported release. Sojourn has already moved to direct remoteexec.kernel ownership, so preserving the duplicate import surface now would freeze an accident.
set.title: P8.D6: Cut client/server/worker dependencies and split the kernel
